## Findings

### Anti-patterns

- vite.config.ts rollup inputs list text-flood as a build entry but nav-data.ts has no corresponding page record. The two registries — build config and navigation data — are the primary synchronization points for page existence, and they are diverged. A page omitted from nav-data.ts will never appear in navigation, prev/next links, or search regardless of whether it builds. [warning] (build-config)
- search.ts line 1 imports `tracks` from nav-data but never uses the symbol anywhere in the file. The 23-entry searchIndex array (lines 11–36) is fully hand-written rather than derived from nav-data, meaning the import conveys false intent and masks that the two registries are completely independent with no shared derivation. [warning] (demo-pages)
- search.ts line 330 uses the deprecated `navigator.platform` API to detect macOS for keyboard shortcut display. The recommended replacement is `navigator.userAgentData.platform` (with `navigator.platform` as a fallback), or a simpler `navigator.userAgent.includes('Mac')` check. [info] (demo-pages)
- text-flood.ts is a navigational orphan: present in src/pages/ and vite.config.ts rollup inputs and sitemap.xml, but absent from nav-data.ts and search.ts. The page builds successfully and is submitted to crawlers, but has no in-site navigation entry point and cannot be found via search. It is discoverable only by direct URL or external link. [info] (demo-pages)
- sitemap.xml includes /pages/text-flood.html, which has no entry in nav-data.ts and no search index entry. Submitting an orphaned page to search engines increases crawl budget consumption for a page users cannot reach through normal navigation, and creates an SEO surface for content that is not part of the defined site structure. [warning] (deployment-assets)
- The codebase has four locations that must agree on the page list: nav-data.ts, vite.config.ts, search.ts searchIndex, and sitemap.xml. text-flood.ts demonstrates these are already out of sync. There is no single authoritative source that the other three derive from — nav-data.ts is the closest candidate but is not consumed by the other three. [warning]
- shell.ts line 52 assumes `t.pages[0]` is the canonical entry point for every track when building header navigation. The non-null assertion (`!`) suppresses the only safety signal. If a track gains a preface or index page at position 0, all header links for that track silently change destination. A `landingHref` field on NavTrack, or a dedicated first-page convention enforced in nav-data, would make the intent explicit. [warning]
- shell.ts lines 111–112 use magic positional indices (`tracks[0]?.pages[2]`, `tracks[4]?.pages[4]`) to look up specific pages for footer links. These lookups fail silently — producing wrong links with no error — if nav-data.ts entries are reordered. nav-data.ts should export a lookup helper keyed on slug so positional fragility is eliminated. [warning]
- search.ts builds its searchIndex with hardcoded absolute href strings (/pages/xxx.html) instead of using the getBase() function exported by nav-data.ts. This makes search result links environment-specific while the rest of the shell correctly adapts to deployment path. The inconsistency means search is silently broken on any non-root deployment. [warning] (site-shell)

### Patterns

- vite.config.ts has zero code-level imports from any internal zone — it contains only declarative path references to HTML entry points. The three-way sync problem (vite.config.ts / search.ts / sitemap.xml) is therefore a maintenance convention gap, not a structural coupling defect, and could be closed by a generation script without touching the module graph. [info] (build-config)
- All 25 non-home demo pages import exclusively from the external @chenglou/pretext library, pretext-helpers, and the components zone — zero imports from site-shell or peer pages. This uniform dependency profile is a clean and intentional architectural constraint worth preserving. [info] (demo-pages)
- pretext-helpers.ts centralizes only the most common pretext operations; demo pages routinely import @chenglou/pretext directly alongside it for specialized APIs. The helper reduces but does not eliminate direct library coupling. Whether a function belongs in the helper vs. called directly is undocumented, leaving future authors to guess the convention. [info] (demo-pages)
- The codebase has no circular dependencies at any layer. The dependency order is strictly: external library → shared utilities → components → demo pages. The one deviation (search.ts in components importing from shared) mirrors the site-shell pattern rather than introducing a cycle. No enforcement mechanism (eslint-plugin-boundaries, tsconfig paths) is in place to preserve this property as the codebase grows. [info]
- The codebase has zero circular dependencies across all zones — every import edge points from consumer pages downward to utilities or outward to the external library. This acyclic topology is a strong architectural property that should be enforced (e.g., via eslint-plugin-import dependency rules) as the page count grows. [info]
- home.ts is the only file that imports from three distinct internal zones (demo-pages utilities, site-shell, newspaper-layout-demo) simultaneously. If home.ts complexity grows, it is the most likely candidate to require its own feature-folder zone to contain the sprawl. [info]
- caveats.ts follows the identical import signature as demo-pages zone files (external lib → pretext-helpers → components), confirming it is architecturally indistinguishable from a demo page at the dependency level — the zone boundary is a community-detection artifact, not a structural one. [info] (pretext-reference-page)
- search.ts line 1 imports `tracks` from nav-data.ts but the symbol is never used in the file. The searchIndex is fully hardcoded. The dead import creates a false signal that search is data-driven from nav-data when it is not, and will cause confusion for any developer attempting to trace how search content is populated. [warning] (site-shell)

### Relationships

- home.ts crosses into the site-shell zone (imports tracks from nav-data.ts) while every other demo page is strictly limited to pretext-helpers and components. This asymmetric coupling makes home.ts an architectural outlier within its own zone and increases the blast radius of any nav-data API change. [warning] (demo-pages)
- home.ts imports `tracks` from nav-data to drive its newspaper column layout, creating a content coupling between the demo and the site's page registry. If nav-data.ts adds, removes, or renames pages or tracks, home.ts rendering is affected — a dependency no other demo page has. This is the only inbound edge from the site-infrastructure layer into a demo page. [warning] (newspaper-layout-demo)
- newspaper-text.ts and newspaper-images.ts are consumed exclusively by home.ts — a strict one-to-one relationship. Their placement in src/shared/ implies shared reuse that does not exist; they are effectively private data modules of the home page. [warning] (newspaper-layout-demo)
- analytics.ts is imported exclusively by shell.ts and has no other consumers — it is a private implementation detail of the site-shell zone, not a shared utility. Its src/shared/ location implies broader reuse that does not exist. [info] (site-shell)
- shell.ts cleanly orchestrates both the shared zone (nav-data) and the components zone (search) using only their public exports. It is the only file in the codebase that spans two architectural tiers within a single import scope, and it does so without accessing internals — a correct and healthy orchestrator pattern. [info] (site-shell)

### Observations

- High cohesion (1) — files are tightly interconnected [info] (bubbles-demo)
- This singleton zone is an algorithmic artifact of community detection — bubbles.ts shares the same architectural pattern as all other demo pages and the separation does not reflect a real design boundary. [info] (bubbles-demo)
- Zero outbound coupling beyond pages-zone imports confirms bubbles.ts follows the expected page isolation pattern with no unexpected shared-state or cross-page dependencies. [info] (bubbles-demo)
- bubbles.ts at 179 lines with hard-coded conversation data and an embedded pretext-vs-fit-content pixel comparison is a well-scoped, self-contained demo — a good reference template for authoring new pages. [info] (bubbles-demo)
- Isolated files — no import edges between 4 files, cohesion is unmeasurable (reported as 0) [info] (build-config)
- Zero cohesion is normal for this zone — .gitignore, LICENSE, llms.txt, and vite.config.ts have no import relationships by nature, so the metric is not meaningful here. [info] (build-config)
- llms.txt at the project root signals intentional LLM-readability documentation — a forward-looking pattern worth keeping current as new pages are added. [info] (build-config)
- vite.config.ts hard-codes all 23 rollup entry points; adding a new page requires edits in at least three places (vite.config.ts, nav-data.ts, sitemap.xml) with no enforcement between them. [warning] (build-config)
- High cohesion (0.96) — files are tightly interconnected [info] (demo-pages)
- Cohesion 0.96 with coupling 0.04 is excellent — pages and their leaf components form a tight, well-bounded cluster reflecting a clean page-owns-its-components pattern. [info] (demo-pages)

### Suggestions

- src/pages/ contains files from 4 zones (bubbles-demo, demo-pages, newspaper-layout-demo, pretext-reference-page) — consider grouping into subdirectories to clarify architectural boundaries [info]
- All 38 page init() functions return silently when the expected DOM element is absent. Adding a single `console.error` (or DEV-only assertion) before the early return would surface template/page mismatches without changing production behavior — a one-line change per file or a shared assert utility. [info]
- The spacing scale in variables.css intentionally skips odd steps above --space-6 (no 7, 9, 11) following a Tailwind-style doubling pattern, but this is undocumented. A comment above the spacing block explaining the scale logic (1–6 are linear 0.25rem steps, then Tailwind T-shirt sizing) would prevent developers from adding --space-7 or similar values that break the intended rhythm. [info]
- Two separate CSS files (global.css line 122 and components.css line 544) independently assign z-index: 1000 to semantically distinct elements (.skip-link and .search-overlay) without any cross-file coordination. Introduce a z-index scale in variables.css so stacking decisions are made in one place and layer relationships are self-documenting. [warning]
- analytics.ts:1 hard-codes the GA measurement ID as a string literal. Replace with `import.meta.env.VITE_GA_ID ?? ''` so the tracking ID is configurable without a source edit and is not committed directly to the repository. [warning]
- Hub function: waitForFonts in src/shared/pretext-helpers.ts is called from 25 files (high fan-in expected for this module type) — changes here have wide impact, consider if responsibilities can be narrowed [info]
- Hub function: createSourceViewer in src/components/source-viewer.ts is called from 23 files — changes here have wide impact, consider if responsibilities can be narrowed [warning]
- 2 potentially unused exports in src/shared/pretext-helpers.ts have no incoming calls: prepareText, measureHeight [info]
- Rollup input keys in vite.config.ts silently mix unquoted identifiers (single-word pages) and quoted kebab-case strings (multi-word pages). The rule follows slug convention but is undocumented. A one-line comment (`// key = page slug; single-word: bare identifier, multi-word: quoted kebab-case`) prevents future inconsistency without any code change. [info] (build-config)
- Zone "Build Configuration" (build-config) has at-risk risk (score: 0.50, cohesion: 0.00, coupling: 0.00) — unreliable: zone has only 4 files (minimum 5 for reliable metrics) [info] (build-config)
- ... and 10 more

## Tooling

This project uses n-dx for codebase analysis (Sourcevision) and requirement
tracking (Rex). MCP tools are available for interactive access to analysis
data and PRD management. Skills available: /plan, /status, /capture,
/zone, /work, /configure.
